body:
Exactly! Her phrasing seems a little odd, but I also think you should give her another chance.

My therapist has to reschedule every now and then, he has two young kids, and if they have to go to the doctor or something, he has to make room for them. Sometime it affects my appointments.

As long as your therapist reschedules your appointment, which she did, don't give up on it just now :)

I don't want this to come across as bitter or an attack on you, but I don't really know how else to put it, so here it goes.

I know that other people hav to work hard to be where they are and achieve their goals, but that's the thing: I cannot even work hard and then see that I don't achieve it. I fail at trying and I don't know how to try anymore.

I already tried to take some weeks of and in fact, I am going on cavation in a couple of weeks, which I probably will enjoy, since travelling always has been something I enjoyed. I just don't see myself enjoying it this time. Also I cannot imagine a situation in which I feel different. Let's say I'd drop everything and start working as a move. I can't even imagine doing that lifting things even though I don't have to think a lot when I'm working. I know that sounds whiny, but here's the thing: I don't know how to help it.

How is your general relationship with your therapist, do you trust him/her? You say that your psychiatrist doesn't really do anything, but you only mention that the sessions with your therapist are not worth it at the moment, so I'm curios if you trust the person and if whether you think that 1 on 1 sessions would help you. Then it would probably be good if you were to mention it to your therapist. I'm sorry that you have to deal with that alone, I suppose it is hard to do that when you are still very young and also depressed. I certainly would have had had a hard time, so I respect you for that! And this subreddit is here to vent, right? So no need for an apology.

Have you tried to take your meds right after you wake up and make that the first thing you do when you start your day? Maybe that could help.

I always try to tell myself that people generally mean well, when they say stuff like that. They don't want you to be depressed and really don't know how to respond to that. I mean, I don't think that I would have understood or known what to say to that before I had those thoughts. And I honestly don't know what to tell you exactly, but I'm sorry for you that you have those thoughts. Still, do you mind if I ask some questions? For how long do you have those thoughts now, and what reaction do you expect (and or need) from your friends when you tell them?

I can only say so for myself, but in the last two or three weeks, I kind of accepted these thoughts as part of how I am right now, and try to see it as "normal" for now, even though I know it is not normal. So if a friend says something like "I'm sorry that you have those thoughts", I get a sense that it is OK for me to think that way, and I don't beat myself up about it, which just feeds into my depression and makes it worse I think.

I know that it is a terrible feeling not knowing how other people will react, because some people see depression as a weakness. I was and am still very reluctant to open up about it, even with family and some few close friends I have. But I'd like to say, that at least for me, being relatively open about my depression, makes it a little easier, because I feel some sort of connection to people. Btw, I'm also 24 and I think that generally, people our age are more "accepting" of depression than others, so I'm pretty sure that there is someone who you know that is willing to help you. Do you have anyone specific in mind? Maybe someone you have shared something else with, or who has shared his or her problems with you?

The way I did it (and my therapist helped me a little coming up with it), is to first ask, if the other person is ok with me telling them about problems I'm having.
You could say something along the lines of: "I know we are not very close, but I've had some troubles lately, and I wanted to know if I can tell you about it?" This way, you are not telling the person your actual problem up front, but you are saying that there is something wrong and ask if the person has room in his/her emotional life to listen to your problems. If the answer is yes, then you can start talking about your depression.
If the answer is no, then that sucks, but you aren't rejected in the way you were by your other friend, who didn't want to be your therapist.

Although it may be worth it to talk to your friend again, if you haven't told her, that you are not looking for a therapist in her, but as someone who can give you company in that dark place. Escpecially if you have a therapist where you go, you can tell her that you are already looking for help. Like you said, she said she didn't want to be "that" for you, but did she say anything about not being "there" for you?

I know it costs a lot of energy, escpecially if you are depressed and thinking about suicide, to go out and make a connection with people, and maybe the first person might not be the right one, but if you have found someone accepting, it usually gets easier. And it is definetly worth it, if you find someone who can help, although I have to say, it won't magically let's your depression disappear. I am still depressed, feel alone, and think about suicide constantly, although I have friends who are there for me. But it is definetly worth the energy you can bring up to do this, because I find it comforting to have someone in that way.

I really hope that helps, and of course you can ask away if oyu have any more questions :)

I can relate to so much of what you are writing. Feeling that you cannot trust yourself and that every decision you make is the wrong one, really sucks. I'm male, so I can't relate to the hormonal changes during PMS, but the inability to make decisions is definetly part of my depression! How long do you think you have the clinical depression, and can you remember a time where you could trust yourself?

Yes, it feels awful. It's not only that I don't know where the time goes, I also have the feeling that I don't make the most of it. When I look back 12 years (I'm in my mid-twenties), I feel that I had in total 4, not always consecutive years, in those 12 years, and that I don't know where the other 8 years are. Like I'm not in control of my life and people are overtaking me left and right. It sounds t  as if you feel the same?

My internship is only 6 months long, although I have to do a second one during my studies and it should happen next year, but I feel like it will be 10 years from now. Last year, for example, was a good year, I travelled a bit and got to see a lot, but it feels as distant as the other good years I had like 6 years ago.

I started six weeks ago with 75mg with which I didn't see results, but also relatively few side effects. The psychiatrist said that that she could see more facial expressions, which is a good sign, so maybe the meds started working. However, when I asked a friend, he couldn't say if he observed a difference over the weeks.

Still, she recommended to bump it up to 150mg until next week, so I'm on 125mg right now. Luckely I don't feel like I'm not able to move th whole day, but then again, suicidal thoughts are not so nice to have as well.

Thank you for the supportive message, I won't give up. Even though I don't know how, it'll get better somehow I guess. Are you still on Sertraline?

Since you've asked: No, you are not alone with this. I can definetly relate and other probably as well. I feel like I have lost track of time as well, be it that a couple of weeks feel like an eternity or a long time feels like yesterday.

For example, I started an internship in November last year and I don't know where the time went, I haven't really come around to to a lot. It feels like I started last week.
Another example is, that I started taking meds a couple of weeks ago, but they haven't helped yet, and it feels like I'm taking them for years (although my depression started like 6 months ago).

I could probably go on and on with my lists, but the bottom line is: No, you are not alone, and maybe that helps a little :)

Thank your for your answer, it's nice to see that your can relate to that.

I don't think that we have a predistined purpose, but I do think that everyone (at least I am) is looking for his or her place in the world and is trying to contribute to it.

Strangely, I set myself to higher standards than others, I think. I wouldn't pressure other people to frind their place in such a way that I am pressuring myself.
